classification.difficultyReason: Infer the tangent gradient from its equation, find two candidate points using differentiation, then select the point on the specified line.

content.prompt: The line $x+y+2=0$ is a tangent to $y=x^3-4x$ at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

answer.worked:
The tangent has equation $y=-x-2$, so its gradient is $-1$.

$$\begin{aligned}y'&=3x^2-4\\-1&=3x^2-4\\3x^2&=3\\x^2&=1\\x&=\pm1\end{aligned}$$

Substitute into the cubic to find the possible coordinates of $P$:

$$\begin{aligned}y(1)&=1^3-4(1)\\&=-3\\y(-1)&=(-1)^3-4(-1)\\&=3\end{aligned}$$

The possible points are $(1,-3)$ and $(-1,3)$. Check them against the specified tangent line:

$$\begin{aligned}1+(-3)+2&=0\\-1+3+2&=4\ne0\end{aligned}$$

Only $(1,-3)$ lies on $x+y+2=0$. Therefore $P(1,-3)$.
